name: Anti-PM/Scl Overlap Syndrome
aliases: Polymyositis-Systemic Sclerosis Overlap with Anti-PM/Scl Antibodies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, serological, and histopathological features

criteria.description: Presence of anti-PM/Scl antibodies in serum
Clinical evidence of polymyositis including proximal muscle weakness and elevated muscle enzymes
Features of systemic sclerosis such as skin thickening, Raynaud phenomenon, or sclerodactyly
Muscle biopsy showing inflammatory myopathy consistent with polymyositis
Abnormal nailfold capillaroscopy findings typical of systemic sclerosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anti-PM/Scl antibodies plus clinical features of both polymyositis and systemic sclerosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of serological, clinical, and histopathological findings; no standardized criteria exist

pathognomonic.notes: Symmetric weakness predominantly affecting shoulder and hip girdles
Localized skin fibrosis typical of systemic sclerosis

common.notes: Vasospastic episodes triggered by cold or stress

occasional.notes: Variable severity; may cause restrictive lung disease
Calcium deposits in skin and subcutaneous tissues
Capillary dropout and dilatation typical of scleroderma
Secondary to lung involvement or vascular disease

laboratory: Presence of anti-PM/Scl antibodies detected by immunoassay
Elevated serum creatine kinase and aldolase
Positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) with nucleolar pattern
imaging: High-resolution CT showing interstitial lung disease
Nailfold capillaroscopy revealing capillary dropout and dilatation
MRI of muscles showing edema and inflammation
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating inflammatory myopathy with lymphocytic infiltrates
Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of systemic sclerosis features such as skin thickening
Absence of significant muscle inflammation or weakness
Negative or different autoantibody profile (e.g., anti-centromere, anti-Scl-70)
Presence of anti-U1 RNP antibodies instead of anti-PM/Scl

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness impairing mobility
Development of severe interstitial lung disease
Signs of renal crisis such as sudden hypertension and renal failure
references: Fischer A, et al. Anti-PM/Scl antibodies: clinical and serological features in systemic sclerosis and polymyositis overlap syndrome. Arthritis Rheum. 2010.
Meyer A, et al. Clinical characteristics and outcome of anti-PM/Scl antibody-positive patients: a multicenter study. Semin Arthritis Rheum. 2015.
Sato S, et al. Clinical features of anti-PM/Scl antibody-positive patients with systemic sclerosis and polymyositis overlap syndrome. J Rheumatol. 2012.
